body:
## Summary

- **Tiered search queries**: Screenplay agent now requires exactly 3 search queries per scene (exact, general, fallback) instead of 1-3 freeform. Reviewer warns when count != 3.
- **Generation prompts**: Added `generation_prompts` (precise + general) to the screenplay visual schema, carried through to script_package for future AI image generation (issue 2.6).
- **Image alignment evaluator**: Replaced inline LLM-based candidate selection in `VisualAssetAgent` with a pluggable `ImageAlignmentEvaluator`. Current implementation is passthrough (first candidate wins); issue 2.6 will add scored rubric evaluation.
- **Broader candidate pool**: `ScriptImageRetrievalAgent` now runs all tiered queries instead of short-circuiting, collecting up to `candidate_pool_factor` × max_candidates before dedup and reranking.

## Accepted regression: LLM image selection → passthrough

This PR removes `_llm_select_best_candidate` from `VisualAssetAgent` and replaces it with a passthrough evaluator that returns the first (pre-ranked) candidate. This is an **accepted quality regression** — the alt-text relevance reranker in `ScriptImageRetrievalAgent` still orders candidates, but the per-scene LLM pick is gone until issue 2.6 adds a scored rubric evaluator.

**Mitigation:** The `alignment_evaluator` is now constructor-injectable on `VisualAssetAgent`, so a custom evaluator (including one that wraps an LLM) can be plugged in without code changes if quality drops before 2.6 lands.

## Files changed

| Screenplay schema | `screenplay_agent.py`, `screenplay_reviewer.py`, `artifacts/screenplay.py` |

body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
This patch addresses an IP spoofing vulnerability in the `getClientIp` function.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
An attacker could bypass rate limiting and other security controls by providing spoofed `X-Real-IP` or `X-Forwarded-For` headers.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
- Prioritizes the platform-verified `request.ip` property (e.g., from Next.js/Vercel).
- Falls back to the **last** entry of the `X-Forwarded-For` header, which is the one appended by the closest trusted proxy.
- Removes trust in the `X-Real-IP` header, as it is non-standard and easily spoofed.
- Updates the call site in the paste API route to pass the full request object.
- Includes comprehensive tests to verify the new secure logic.

Fixes #32725

The flamegraph SVG had a fixed pixel `height` attribute, which combined
with the `viewBox` aspect ratio, caused the browser to constrain the
rendered width — leaving the right side of the viewport empty.

- Changed `height="{image_height}"` → `height="100%"` on the `<svg>` element
- Added `fg:content_height="{image_height}"` to `<g id="frames">` so the
  JS resize logic can still reference the original content height
- Updated `flamegraph.js` to read `orig_height` from the new attribute
- Added test assertions for the new attributes

`ensure_logged_in_moodle` was failing with `TimeoutException` — 30 s wasn't enough to detect courses or guest access, and there was no visibility into what the browser was actually showing.

## Changes

- **Timeout**: `WAIT_SEC` 30 → 60 s
- **Logging**: module-level `logging` + `log` throughout every SSO/login stage (`maybe_login_nidp`, `ensure_on_moodle`, `click_login_if_guest`, `ensure_logged_in_moodle`, `get_courses`, `main`) — current URL, what was clicked, course counts, etc.
- **Debug screenshots**: `take_debug_screenshot(driver, name)` saves `/tmp/debug_<name>_<ts>.png`; called automatically at every timeout/failure point
- **Retry with exponential backoff**: `_retry_with_backoff(func, retries, initial_delay)` — used in the fallback SSO path of `ensure_logged_in_moodle` (2 retries, 3 s initial delay, doubles each attempt)
- **Broader course selectors**: `_collect_course_anchors` now tries 6 CSS selectors instead of one, deduped by href, to handle theme variations:

      "[data-courseid] a",

## Summary
This PR renames the project from "PerformOS" to "Bord" and removes legacy standalone scripts in favor of the unified FastAPI-based architecture. The core analytics and dashboard generation logic is preserved while consolidating the codebase.

## Key Changes

### Branding & Naming
- Updated all references from "PerformOS" to "Bord" across documentation, configuration files, and source code
- Modified `pyproject.toml` to reflect new project name and description
- Updated comments and docstrings throughout the codebase

### Script Consolidation
- **Removed legacy standalone scripts:**
  - `health_analyzer.py` (1118 lines) — core health analysis logic now integrated into pipeline
  - `cockpit_server.py` (625 lines) — replaced by FastAPI-based `api/main.py`
  - `server_simple.py` — simplified launcher removed
  - Multiple shell launchers (`run.command`, `Lancer_PerformOS.command`, `launch_simple.sh`, etc.)
  - Setup/installation scripts (`install_schedule.sh`, `setup_autorun.sh`, `reset_performos.sh`, `setup_desktop.sh`)
  - Diagnostic scripts (`diagnose.py`, `diagnose_sync.py`, `test_launch.py`)
  - Desktop app creation scripts (`create_app.sh`, `create_simple_app.sh`, `create_desktop_shortcut.sh`)

### Frontend Refactoring
- Extracted reusable UI components:
  - `LoadingSpinner` component for consistent loading states
  - `ErrorCard` component for error handling
  - `MetricPill` component for metric display
  - `EventList` component for planner events
  - `BoardKanban` component for task management
- Added shared utilities in `frontend/lib/utils.ts` for color mapping and date formatting
- Updated page components (`semaine`, `sante`, `travail`, `social`) to use new shared components

body:
### 💡 What
1. **Concurrency Upgrade:** Switched FastAPI endpoints in `cases.py`, `rules.py`, and `predict.py` from `async def` to `def`.
2. **Database Query Optimization:** Replaced separate data and counting queries with a single query using `.select("*", count="exact")` on Supabase pagination endpoints.

### 🎯 Why
- **FastAPI Threading:** The codebase makes heavy use of the *synchronous* `supabase-py` client and performs CPU-bound ML inferences using `XGBoost/LightGBM`. When these are housed within `async def` endpoints, they block FastAPI's single event loop, severely degrading concurrent request handling. Changing them to `def` automatically offloads these operations to an external thread pool.
- **N+1 Pagination:** Fetching paginated lists previously took two distinct database roundtrips (one for the slice of data, one for the total count). This optimization combines them into one, halving the database overhead and latency.

### 📊 Impact
- Substantially improves concurrency and unblocks the main event loop under load.
- Reduces database roundtrips by 50% for all list API endpoints (`/api/cases` and `/api/rules`).

### 🔬 Measurement
To verify the optimizations:
1. Run the test suite: `pytest backend/`
2. Test the API: Check `total` counts are correctly returned when hitting `/api/cases` or `/api/rules` via the UI or `curl`.
3. Read the journal: Review the new architectural learnings in `.jules/bolt.md`.

🛡️ **Sentinel: [HIGH] Fix Privilege Escalation in Registration**

🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Mass Assignment / Privilege Escalation in `AuthHandler.Register`.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could register a new account and explicitly set their role to `admin` by including a `role` field in the JSON request body. This would grant them full administrative access to the system.
🔧 **Fix:** 
- Modified the registration request payload struct to exclude the `Role` field.

| Error Type | Safe Message | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `StateCorruptedError` | State storage error. Craig will attempt recovery. | `STATE_ERROR` |
| `ConfigNotFoundError` | Configuration not found. Run craig_config to set up. | `CONFIG_ERROR` |
| `ConfigValidationError` | Configuration is invalid. Check your craig.yaml. | `CONFIG_ERROR` |
| `ConfigParseError` | Configuration file could not be parsed. | `CONFIG_ERROR` |

author: robinandreeklund-collab
body:
## Summary

This PR replaces the planned Riksbank MCP server integration with a new SMHI (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute) MCP server integration. The plan has been completely rewritten to focus on weather, hydrology, oceanography, and fire risk data from SMHI's Open Data APIs instead of Swedish economic data from Riksbank.

## Key Changes

- **Scope shift**: From 8 economic tools (interest rates, currency, forecasts) to 10 weather/environmental tools across 6 categories (weather forecasts, weather analysis, weather observations, hydrology, oceanography, fire risk)
- **API endpoints**: Changed from 3 Riksbank APIs (SWEA, SWESTR, Forecasts) to 9 SMHI APIs (metfcst, snow1g, mesan2g, metobs, hydroobs, pthbv, ocobs, fwif1g, fwia)
- **Authentication**: Removed API key requirement (SMHI APIs are fully open)
- **Project structure**: Maintained identical pattern to riksbank-mcp but with SMHI-specific tools and schemas
- **Tool definitions**: Replaced economic tools with weather/environmental tools (e.g., `smhi_vaderprognoser_metfcst`, `smhi_hydrologi_hydroobs`, `smhi_brandrisk_fwif`)
- **Skill file**: Changed from `swedish-economy` to `swedish-weather` with weather-related triggers
- **Port assignment**: Changed from port 3103 to port 3005 (internal) / 3104 (local Docker)
- **Caching strategy**: Differentiated TTLs based on update frequency (30 min for forecasts, 5 min for observations)

## Implementation Details

- All SMHI APIs use standard JSON responses (no XML parsing needed)
- Tools accept geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude) for point-based queries or parameter/station IDs for observations
- Comprehensive Zod schemas for SMHI data types (forecasts, observations, analyses)
- Markdown formatting for weather data tables and summaries
- Integration with existing docker-compose and combined-mcp infrastructure
- Swedish language throughout (descriptions, instructions, error messages)

author: copilot
body:
The APK had four bugs preventing its core proxy/interception functionality from working at all.

## Bugs Fixed

### Critical: VPN routing loop (`ProxyVpnService`)
`handlePacket()` wrote raw TUN packets back to the TUN file descriptor, re-injecting them into the VPN network indefinitely. No traffic ever reached a real server.

- Replaced echo-back with `VpnService.Builder.setHttpProxy(ProxyInfo.buildDirectProxy("localhost", port))` on API 29+ so apps honouring the system proxy route HTTP/HTTPS directly to `localhost:9090` over loopback
- `processPackets()` now just drains the TUN fd to keep the VPN connection alive
- Removed dead `handlePacket()` method

### Critical: Proxy outbound sockets not VPN-exempt (`ProxyServer`)
Proxy connections to real servers were captured by `addRoute("0.0.0.0", 0)` and looped back through the VPN.

- Added `vpnService: VpnService? = null` to `ProxyServer`
- `vpnService?.protect(socket)` called before `connect()` in `forwardHttpsRequest`, `handleHttp`, and `tunnelConnection`
- `ProxyVpnService` passes `this` to `ProxyServer`

### Scope/compilation bug in `handleHttp`
`entry` was declared inside `try { }` but referenced in `catch { }` — not in scope per Kotlin/JVM scoping rules.

```kotlin
// Before (broken)
try {
    val entry = TrafficEntry(...)
} catch (e: Exception) {
    trafficRepository.updateEntry(entry.id) { ... }  // Unresolved reference
}

// After
var entry: TrafficEntry? = null
try {
    entry = TrafficEntry(...)
} catch (e: Exception) {
    entry?.let { trafficRepository.updateEntry(it.id) { ... } }
}
```

### Dead code / resource leak in `handleMitmConnection`
`sslServerSocket` was opened on a random port and `localPort` captured, but neither was used. The MITM path wraps `clientSocket` directly. Both removed.

## Tests Added
`ProxyServerTest` covers entry state transitions (`PENDING → COMPLETE/FAILED`) and the null-entry guard pattern from the `handleHttp` fix.

author: congregalis
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a minimal-intrusion refactor for LLM provider integration by centralizing provider metadata and client dispatch logic into a provider registry, while keeping existing call sites and APIs compatible.

It also adds first-class support for:
- OpenAI Responses API (`openai-response`)
- Gemini native API (`gemini`)

## Why

Provider-specific logic was previously spread across multiple constants and condition branches, which made adding new providers error-prone and harder to maintain.

This refactor aims to:
- Keep existing runtime behavior stable for current providers
- Make new provider onboarding predictable and low-risk
- Improve observability for provider-level failures

## What Changed

- Added provider registry and metadata model in `llm_client`:
  - canonical provider definitions
  - alias normalization
  - capability/default URL/max token metadata
  - manifest export for UI consumption

- Refactored provider client creation to use registry-driven dispatch in `create_llm_client(...)`.

- Added `OpenAIResponsesClient`:
  - request/response mapping for `/v1/responses`
  - tool-call normalization to unified response format
  - fixed error handling to avoid false positives on `error: null`
  - fallback parsing for `output_text` when output blocks are empty

- Added `GeminiClient` (native API):
  - supports `generateContent` and `streamGenerateContent`
  - message/tool conversion between unified format and Gemini format
  - vision input handling for inline base64 image content
  - compatibility fallback to OpenAI-compatible behavior for legacy `/openai` Gemini gateways

- Added new endpoint:
  - `GET /enterprise/llm-providers`
  - returns provider manifest/capabilities for frontend/provider selection

- Updated enterprise settings frontend:
  - provider options are now loaded from `/enterprise/llm-providers`
  - retains local fallback provider list for resilience

- Improved LLM error logging in websocket path:
  - provider/model/round context added for faster diagnosis

## Compatibility / Impact

- No change to existing `llm-models` CRUD contract.
- Existing call path (`create_llm_client(...).complete/stream`) remains unchanged at call sites.
- Existing providers remain supported.
- `codex` and `claude-code` providers are intentionally removed from registry scope in this PR to reduce complexity.

## Validation

Executed successfully:

- `python3 -m compileall backend/app/services/llm_client.py backend/app/services/llm_utils.py backend/app/api/enterprise.py backend/app/api/websocket.py`
- `npm run build` (frontend)

## Notes

- `OpenAIResponsesClient.stream` currently uses a minimal non-tokenized streaming fallback strategy (functional and stable, but not token-by-token native streaming yet).
- Follow-up enhancements can further optimize response streaming behavior if needed.

author: paoloirrera
body:
Split the monolithic `lib/` directory into distinct top-level folders:
- `src/` for shared runtime code (Lambda functions, Docker, React app)
- `iac-cdk/` for CDK infrastructure-as-code constructs
- `iac-terraform/` for Terraform infrastructure-as-code (new)
- `bin/` moved under `iac-cdk/bin/`

Update Makefile to support both CDK and Terraform build workflows, and adjust .gitignore, CONTRIBUTING.md, and all import paths to reflect the new directory layout. This enables multi-IaC support while cleanly separating application code from infrastructure.
